reason: The recheck holds. It confirms a decision already made, so it adds no new mechanism, needs no OK and does not conflict with R1-R10. Evidence checked: (1) #34 was submitted 25 Sep 08:09:00Z and scored 0.953 (CONTEXT l.1797). On 25 Sep 11:27Z there were 241 teams at 0.953 (l.1550). With scoring latency of at least 6.3 h, all of them were submitted before about 05:00Z, which is before #34. The tie rule is Rules §3.7.b, 'entered first' (l.1798 ff). Late copies sit at the end of the block (l.2033), and our kernels are deterministic run to run (l.796). So #34 is at least about 240th in its copy block. (2) Snapshot 17:01Z: 0.953 block = 354 teams (ranks 296-649). Forecast l.2324: 250-400 teams above X, bronze line about 395. That puts #34 at about rank 490-640, as the finding claims. (3) World check (mine): {#37,#34} and {#37,#38} differ only when the insertion is below 0 on private. There #34 beats the twin only if lowrefine is at or below 0 (at exactly 0 the twin loses the tie, because it was submitted on 26 Sep 00:02, after #34). Even then #34 medals only if 155 or fewer teams beat X on private. The joint probability is under about 1%. The twin alone wins the world 'insertion < 0, lowrefine > 0' (P about 0.07-0.10) at rank about 250-400. So #34 is dominated. Two small overstatements, neither changes the verdict: 'beyond bronze in essentially every world' fails in the small-field world (#34 about 390-440, borderline), and '~#200-300 of ~350' is a lower-bound estimate, because LastSubmissionDate in the CSV is not the time of the scoring submission. For RC-A the lesson carries over only in kind. A successor published on 27-28 Sep would collect far fewer copies than x138's ~350 by the deadline, so the bottom-of-block penalty for a verbatim port is smaller than this arithmetic suggests. Hardware nondeterminism across copy holders would blur the block, but #34 would still land mid-block (rank about 425-575).
fix: None for the finals. #37 + #38 stay as ticked, with the rule 'Never tick #34, #35, P36 or two files with identical components'. When this is cited in the round-11 successor analysis: (a) say 'beyond bronze in all but the small-field world (<=~155 teams above X)'; (b) scale the bottom-of-block penalty for a successor port by the successor's expected copy count at the deadline, not by x138's 354.
realistic_gain: 0 on public and on private. It confirms the current finals. Its value is the documented tie arithmetic (the late-copy penalty), used as qualitative support for 'successor + insertion' over a verbatim port in R11-RC-A. Cost: none.
